facts.text: Maricopa Colony’s heart is the Historical Society Museum and Visitor Center on Maricopa‑Casa Grande Highway, where local history comes alive.
In 1879 Maricopa Wells dropped its second name and moved its post office south to link with the Southern Pacific Railroad.
Monthly, the Maricopa Historical Society meets in the Redwood Room of the new Library, inviting speakers to share stories of the town.
During the 1850s and 1860s, Maricopa Wells served as a major stagecoach relay for the San Antonio‑San Diego and Butterfield Overland Mail Lines.
Heritage Park hosts the Maricopa Museum and Visitor Center, once home to a historic water tower that anchors field‑trip tours.
